_about: Electrification configurations of Padullés et al. (2026), Sec. 4.3. Each value is tagged: 'published' = stated in the paper text or tables; 'figure' = read from a figure (uncertainty given); 'assumed' = our assumption, with the reason. Energy in kWh/hl, temperatures in °C.

eta_lorenz.where: Sec. 4.3.1, Eq. (1), citing Andersen et al. [41]

cold_utility_T_C.where: Sec. 4.1 and 4.3.1 (minimum T* of the GCC)

config_1_cchs.description: Central HTHP for simultaneous heating and cooling (CCHS) replacing the boiler and chiller.

Q_sink_with_HR.where: Sec. 4.3.2 and 7: external heat after Pfaduko and wort-cooling heat recovery

sink.reason: isothermal steam utility at the swept temperature (Fig. 11 x-axis)

source_T_C.reason: cold utility temperature; the paper also uses ambient but does not split the source duty

W_published_text.where: Sec. 4.3.1 and 7: 'reduce electricity consumption to 5 kWh/hl if steam is supplied at the minimum viable pressure'

config_2_two_hp.description: CO2 heat pump for the warm-water heat recovery tank plus HTHP for wort boiling; Pfaduko kept.

units.name: CO2 HP
units.tags: Q_sink, sink temperatures, W: published (Fig. 14); COP 3.5: published (Sec. 4.3.2); source -1 °C: assumed (cold utility)

units.name: HTHP
units.tags: Q_sink, W: published (Fig. 14); COP 2: published (Sec. 4.3.2); sink 103 °C: assumed (GCC maximum T*, needed for wort boiling); source -1 °C: assumed

config_3_fully_integrated.description: CO2 heat pump (warm water), MVR for wort boiling, booster for wort preheating and MVR start-up (electric boiler or HTHP).
